paragraphs: Rav Mesharshiya, grandson of Rav Acha bar Rav.
In Sanhedrin 77a there is a dispute between Ravina and Rav Acha bar Rav [who exempts]. Rav Mesharshiya said: “What is the reason of my grandfather, who exempts?” etc.

And in Chullin 49a, Rav Ada bar Natan said we may rely on it (the reading Hyman reports from Dikdukei Soferim is Rav Acha bar Rav, and so it is in the Ran, and in Rashi too it reads Rav Acha). Mar Zutra son of Rav Mari said we may not rely on it. Rav Mesharshiya said to him: The view of my grandfather is the more reasonable.

And in Chullin 67b we find that Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Acha said to Ravina; and Hyman says it must read Rav Mesharshiya, the grandson of Rav Acha, for Hyman identifies this Ravina as the last Ravina, whose father is abbreviated ר״ה here, and says that he was orphaned of his father, as they say there that Ravina said to his mother: Hide them for me, and I will eat. It was concerning this that Rav Mesharshiya raised a difficulty against Ravina. So too is the opinion of Dor ha-Rishonim part 3, p. 50, that it must read 'grandson'.

And Hyman considers it possible that this Rav Mesharshiya is the one mentioned in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 4: that in the year 781 (תשפ״א), on Shabbat, in Tevet, were arrested Rabbana Ameimar bar Mar Yenuka, and Huna bar Mar Zutra the Exilarch, and Mesharshiya bar Pakod, and they were killed on the 18th of it. And in Sefer ha-Kabbalah of the Ra'avad he is mentioned by the name Rav Mesharshiya.
